entities.name: The Transformation
entities.tagline: Every man-made structure on Earth collapses at once. Everyone indoors dies.

beats.headline: January 3rd
beats.text: It takes a minute. Then the System AI makes a planet-wide announcement opening Dungeon Crawler World: Earth, and staircases appear. The survivors are, almost without exception, the people who happened to be outside at the time — which is why the cast of this series is so weighted toward smokers, insomniacs and people chasing a pet.

entities.name: Eighteen Floors, On a Clock
entities.tagline: Every floor runs on a timer. When it expires the floor collapses with everyone still on it.

beats.headline: The deal
beats.text: Reach the bottom and humanity gets Earth back. Almost nobody is expected to. The clock is the one rule the dungeon never bends, because the collapse is the show's season structure.

beats.headline: The difficulty cliff at floor four
beats.text: The early floors are deliberately built to drown crawlers in low-tier loot and beginner skills. From the fourth floor on, boxes and achievements get dramatically harder to come by — the point where the show stops subsidising its cast.

entities.name: Dungeon Crawler World
entities.tagline: The crawl is a television programme broadcast across the galaxy. The survivors are the cast.

beats.headline: Ratings are currency
beats.text: Ratings buy sponsors; sponsors send gold and loot; gold and loot buy another floor of life. Being entertaining is a survival stat, and production will bend the dungeon itself to get a better episode.

beats.headline: The audience can be turned
beats.text: The Hunting Grounds prove the format cuts both ways. A broadcast that humiliates the people who paid for it is still a broadcast, and production cannot switch it off without admitting why.

entities.name: Loot Boxes
entities.tagline: Six tiers: Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Legendary, Celestial — each dramatically rarer than the last.

beats.headline: Where boxes come from
beats.text: Achievements, bosses (Boss Boxes, scaling with the boss's rank), quests (Quest Boxes), and viewers (Fan Boxes and Benefactor Boxes). Boxes stay locked in the Awards and Boxes tab until the crawler reaches a safe room or guildhall, and then it is all-or-nothing — every accumulated box opens in sequence, lowest tier first.

beats.headline: The tiers cost the house real money
beats.text: Borant owes the Syndicate a tax on the tier of every non-sponsored box it awards, which is why the top tiers are so vanishingly rare. Across the entire history of the show only 2,145 Celestial boxes have ever been given out, and no single crawler has ever received more than four. Drops key to a crawler's race rather than their class, so a barbarian can easily end up holding a necromancer's staff.

beats.headline: Benefactor Boxes break the theme
beats.text: Only patrons can send them, and they are the one category that ignores the dungeon's fantasy dressing — a pulse rifle, powered armour, gear from the sponsor's own homeworld. A Bronze Benefactor Box outclasses a plain Gold Adventurer Box.

beats.headline: The Celestial veto
beats.text: At the end of the third floor a quest reward is double-upgraded all the way to Celestial for 83 crawlers. Borant spends its single per-season veto to negate the prizes — but not before the crawler Quan Ch opens his, leaving Borant liable for it and triggering an expensive Syndicate court fight. The upgrade achievements responsible are patched out immediately.

entities.name: Compensated Anarchist
entities.tagline: A unique monk/rogue hybrid. Trapmaker, bomb-maker, social-media dynamo.

beats.headline: The system's own description
beats.text: "Will happily throw a Molotov through a window one moment and step in front of a camera to plead for the violence to stop the next." Carl takes it alongside the Primal race at class selection on the third floor.

beats.headline: Agent Provocateur
beats.text: The bomb-focused specialisation, taken on the sixth floor.

entities.name: Former Child Actor
entities.tagline: A bard/rogue class that lets her pick a new class at every single level.

beats.headline: Taken with the Cat race on the third floor
beats.text: Her constitution is far too low for melee, so she fights on charisma and spells. The per-level class pick is what turns her into a jack-of-all-trades rather than a novelty — and the reason a show cat ends up out-scaling most of the human crawlers.

entities.name: The Desperado Club
entities.tagline: The crawlers-only bar that persists between floors. Bouncer, house rules, and a stage.

beats.headline: Entry is a tattoo
beats.text: Access comes with a Desperado Pass Tattoo — Carl's on his neck, Donut's on her right shoulder blade, glowing gold through the fur. It is the one place crawlers can reliably coordinate, which makes it the most dangerous room in the dungeon for the people running the show.

beats.headline: Hiring out of the Desperado
beats.text: On the fourth floor Carl and Donut hire Bomo and The Sledge out of the club and meet up with Elle and Imani there. It stops being a bar the moment it becomes a labour market.

entities.name: The NPCs Are People
entities.tagline: The dungeon's 'non-player characters' are populations with histories, families and scripts written for them.

beats.headline: The bubbles are inhabited
beats.text: The fifth floor's pocket worlds hold whole civilisations — the Necropolis of Anser, the pazuzu town of Pandinus, a colony of dirigible gnomes — that were living there before any crawler arrived and will be there after.

beats.headline: Signet has a writers' room
beats.text: Tsarina Signet is the protagonist of a scripted Syndicate drama, Vengeance of the Daughter, with producers steering her grief and her vengeance for the audience. She is not a person the dungeon generated. She is a person the dungeon is doing this to.

beats.headline: Juice Box tells them
beats.text: Under cover of the Larracos flood, Juice Box hides among the survivors and spreads word of what the NPCs truly are. It is the single most consequential thing anyone does on the ninth floor.

beats.headline: They organise
beats.text: Floor 9's NPCs form their own independent tenth faction. No season has ever recorded it, and the system has no procedure for it.

entities.name: Death Is Final Here
entities.tagline: On the ninth floor there are no respawns and no loopholes.

beats.headline: Thirty days, nine armies, one castle
beats.text: Roughly 32,000 conscripted crawlers and 50,000 retired ones against something like 100,000 armed enemies, fighting for Larracos at the centre of the map. Everything the series has spent six books making you care about is on a board where nothing comes back.
